ECO-11. NDC7002N VGS(th) is 1.0/1.9/2.5 V max and Q10A must sink ~14 uA through the TPS3840's 100 kOhm internal MR pull-up at VGS ~= 2.0 V, Q10B runs at 0.990 x SW, and Q9B opens the low-battery LED at /D1A ~= 3.0 V. A worst-case part is at or below threshold in all three, so the brownout latch may never arm and the low-battery LED may never light -- invisibly, since the console works normally until the protection was meant to act. FDC6301N is 0.65/0.85/1.5 V max on the identical SUPERSOT-6 land with the same pin assignment, giving >=0.5 V of worst-case overdrive everywhere. Its asymmetric -0.5 V gate rating is covered by its own integrated gate-source Zener ('>6 kV HBM'), whose clamp current at Q10A's power-up excursion is set by R16 -- which ECO-8 had already raised from 10k to 100k, making it 25 uA. Headroom: 25 V / 0.22 A against 5.0 V and <=165 uA.

VGS(th) max 2.5 V with no RDS(on) spec below VGS = 4.5 V. Fine for Q2/Q5/Q7, whose gates are driven to 3.23-5.0 V. Q9 and Q10 moved to the FDC6301N by ECO-11 because their gate drive is BELOW this threshold -- see that document.

ECO-13, and the reason this repository exists. On the AGBM-01 base U2 was a salvaged AGB-SRAM off a donor console, and ECO-5 was OUR unverified attempt to let a new part stand in for it. AGBM-02 carries MouseBiteLabs' own dual land, so this is simply an ORDERABLE PART: the machine buys it and places it, and a build needs exactly one chip off a donor -- the CPU. His Required Parts page: "For the AGBM-02 and AGBM-12, you *only* need the CPU." Tape-and-reel suffix chosen over the tube part for machine placement. 8 Mbit 512K x 16 async SRAM, 45 ns, 48-TSOP I. TWO HAND STEPS COME WITH IT and no assembly line does either: bridge JP2 (U2 pin 17 MA17 to GND) and JP3 (pin 47 /BYTE to VDD2 for x16 word mode). Leave BOTH open if you fit a salvaged OEM AGB-SRAM instead -- the land still accepts it, and then this line comes off the BOM. $10.85, 1,695 in stock, verified 2026-08-19.
